overview: This uint8 enum selects which gamepad motor groups a damage feedback pulse drives.

None.simple: No controller-side channel change is requested.
None.technical: The row constructor defaults ForceFeedbackChannel to None. PlayForceFeedback resolves the preset Id in ForceFeedbackDataTables and passes the row value to PlayForceFeedbackPulse. That switch has no None case, so the switch default leaves the freshly constructed FForceFeedbackChannelDetails with all four motor flags enabled. No exported preset uses None.

Left.simple: Only the left side of the gamepad vibrates.
Left.technical: PlayForceFeedbackPulse clears bAffectsRightLarge and bAffectsRightSmall, leaving the left large and small motor flags untouched. It then builds a flat FRichCurve with Power at times 0 and Duration and calls PlayForceFeedback for the requested player. No exported preset uses Left.

Right.simple: Only the right side of the gamepad vibrates.
Right.technical: PlayForceFeedbackPulse clears bAffectsLeftLarge and bAffectsLeftSmall, leaving the right large and small motor flags untouched. It then builds the same flat Power curve over 0 and Duration and calls PlayForceFeedback. No exported preset uses Right.

All.simple: Both sides of the gamepad vibrate.
All.technical: All is the channel on every one of the 11 exported ForceFeedback presets. PlayForceFeedbackPulse has no All case, so the switch default leaves all four motor flags enabled. Power and Duration from the same row become a two-key flat FRichCurve, and the battle damage caller passes player 0.

Invalid.simple: An out-of-range marker that behaves like the all-channel preset.
Invalid.technical: PlayForceFeedbackPulse has no Invalid case, so an out-of-range value reaches the same default branch as All and leaves all four motor flags enabled. The preset exports contain no Invalid row, so this behavior is traced only through the factory switch.

notes: Left and Right name the two motor groups. The reconstructed pulse function clears only the flags for the opposite side.
None, All and Invalid all take the same default branch, which keeps every motor flag enabled.
Power and Duration come from the same ForceFeedback row and are shared by all channels. The battle damage caller hard-codes player 0.
All 11 exported ForceFeedback presets use All, so the other four members have no exported data example.
AInputManager::PlayForceFeedback checks the global enabled flag and player indices before replacing the transient effect channel.
